title: Critical: Unauthenticated HTTP MCP endpoint with CORS wildcard
description: mcp_http.c POST /mcp and GET /mcp accept any request with no authn/authz, origin validation, CSRF protection, or per-client authorization. Since MCP tools trigger input actions on the host desktop, this is a remote code execution vector if bound beyond localhost. Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is sent for all responses. max_clients config is declared but never used; hardcoded MAX_SSE_CLIENTS 4 controls capacity.
close_reason: fixed

title: Critical: PipeWire frame buffer leak and data race in on_process()
description: capture_pipewire.c:604-610 on_process() overwrites pending_frame/held_pw_buf if a previous frame is still unreleased. The old PipeWire buffer is never requeued, causing buffer starvation/leak and data lifetime races. Also pw_stop() does not signal frame_cond before join (line 814-826), blocking get_frame(). Init failure paths (710-726) leak partially-created core/stream/portal resources.
close_reason: Closed

title: client: overlay+video use two separate SDL_RenderPresent calls -> ghost trails + mis-scaled video
description: on_decoded() calls md_renderer_present() (clear+copy video+present) while the main loop's render_client_overlay()->render_draw_data() does a second SDL_RenderPresent() after drawing ImGui, with no clear or video redraw. On a double-buffered SDL_Renderer the two present sources flip-book: moving the overlay leaves ghost trails of its prior positions, and the visible buffer alternates between a full video frame and a stale/half-scaled one (remote desktop appears shrunk to the top-left quarter on HiDPI). Fix: one render pass per frame — begin(clear+copy video at scale 1) -> draw overlay -> single present.
close_reason: Fixed and verified live: video fills window, single-present (no trails), restore_token skips consent, mouse/keyboard forwarded (remote cursor tracks + hover responds, host rx grows)

title: host: capture thread exits before PipeWire stream reaches STREAMING (frames=0, black screen)
description: capture_thread_func()'s loop guard is md_capture_is_active(), which is only true once on_state_changed sees PW_STREAM_STATE_STREAMING. host_wait_capture_dimensions() returns as soon as on_param_changed sets width/height (during format negotiation, before STREAMING), so the thread is spawned while active is still false and exits immediately — the stream delivers frames into pending_frame but nobody consumes them (host frames=0 sent=0, client black screen). Reproduced cross-host: Mac client ↔ Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME Wayland VM; link active, format BGRx 1512x909 negotiated, yet 0 frames. Native fast Linux usually wins the race. Fix: capture thread waits up to ~5s for active before its pull loop.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

title: host: odd capture dimensions (e.g. 1512x909) make encoder creation fail
description: md_encoder_create() rejects odd width/height (NV12 needs even), and host/main.c passes the raw capture dimensions straight through, so a display with an odd edge — observed with a 1512x909 GNOME session in a UTM VM — aborts the host with 'failed to create encoder'. Fix: round encoder dims down to even; accept capture frames up to 1 px larger in the frame-size check (md_encoder_submit already crops via the caller stride); keep true display size for input injection.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

title: host dies with SIGPIPE on Linux when a client disconnects mid-send
description: On Linux a client that closes immediately after connect (e.g. a port probe) makes the host's initial UI-tree send hit a closed socket; write() raises SIGPIPE and metadesk-host is killed (observed on Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64; ssh reported exit 255 = signal). macOS masks this via SO_NOSIGPIPE semantics. Fix: ignore SIGPIPE in host/client main (and/or use MSG_NOSIGNAL in stream.c sends) and treat EPIPE as connection lost.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

title: capture_pipewire: SelectSources sends persist_mode as boolean; portal method errors ignored

Also portal_wait_response() discards method-error replies, hiding the cause. Fix: send uint32 0; log and fail fast on DBUS_MESSAGE_TYPE_ERROR.

title: a11y: push events discarded, full desktop re-walk under the backend lock
description: atspi_change_event_cb (a11y_atspi.c:282), axui_observer_cb (a11y_axui.m:470) and UIAChangeHandler::emit_change (a11y_uia.cpp:602) all (void) the event payload and call get_diff_unlocked while holding the lock, re-walking the whole desktop over IPC. macOS subscribes kAXValueChanged, which fires per keystroke. Build deltas from the event (element/notification/changeType/runtimeId), coalesce with a debounce timer, never hold the lock across IPC. See docs/reviews/slop-audit-media.md finding A3.
acceptance_criteria: a single focus change does not trigger a full-desktop walk; no lock held across a cross-process call
notes: Audit re-verified 2026-09-21. Acceptance #2 (no lock held across cross-process call) is ALREADY satisfied in all three backends: atspi_change_event_cb, axui_observer_cb, and UIAChangeHandler::emit_change each capture cb under the lock, unlock, THEN call md_a11y_diff (see the 'Diff outside the backend lock' comments; landed with md-0uf/md-h82). Remaining = acceptance #1 only: each event still triggers a full-desktop md_a11y_diff. Correct fix is per-platform subtree deltas built from the event payload (AtspiEvent.source/type/detail1; AXUIElementRef+notification; IUIAutomationElement+runtimeId) plus a get_subtree backend seam and burst coalescing. This is genuinely platform-specific and only the macOS (AXUI) backend is buildable on the current darwin host; atspi (Linux) and uia (Windows) need per-OS CI to land safely. Deferring rather than shipping a blind, unverifiable threaded coalescer + 3-backend rewire (would violate the audit's 'no unverifiable complexity' rule). Keep P1.
close_reason: Merged to master as b530596 (d6c46e3, 0c612ad, 9c631c6, 9b65950). Acceptance #1 met platform-neutrally: backends dispatch a change HINT (md_a11y_change_dispatch) with no md_a11y_diff/get_tree per event; MCP consumer invalidates the lazy snapshot and emits one coalesced notifications/resources/updated per burst (50ms quiet / 200ms cap, bounded retry). Seed walks on subscribe removed. Verified: 22/22 unit, MCP suites x10 serial, ASan clean, live macOS 1 hint -> 0 get_tree. a11y_atspi.c syntax-checked; a11y_uia.cpp edit mechanical and UNCOMPILED (needs Windows build). Per-platform subtree deltas from event payload remain deferred — only needed for consumers wanting pushed content, none exist today.

title: ipc_win32: first accept() timeout ignored - missing FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED

title: Windows live UIA run: newline labels break compact format; UIA control-type gaps + Header→HEADING mis-map
description:
Why: the first interactive Windows desktop walk through metadesk (UTM Win11 ARM64, 250 nodes, atspi_dump --compact) surfaced: (1) labels containing CR/LF (taskbar Clock 'Clock 4:51 PM\n<LRM>11/16/2026', OneDrive and Network tray buttons; 3 labels) are emitted verbatim by compact_node(), so a single node spills across lines and the line-based compact format (spec §3.3.2) becomes ambiguous — platform-neutral, any backend can produce multi-line accessible names. (2) 5 nodes with role 'unknown': a11y_uia.cpp MD_UIA_ROLES lacks Thumb, Separator, TitleBar, HeaderItem, Calendar, Custom, AppBar, SemanticZoom. (3) UIA_HeaderControlTypeId is mapped to MD_A11Y_ROLE_HEADING, but UIA Header is the container of HeaderItems (column header row), not a heading — same class of bug as the AT-SPI 'header' alias fixed in md-eiy. Encoding was verified correct (UTF-8 C2 B0 / E2 80 8E bytes); the garbling seen was PowerShell 5.1 display only.

What: (a) compact serializer: replace control characters (< 0x20, incl. CR/LF/TAB) in labels with a single space; JSON unchanged (cJSON escapes). Unit test. (b) UIA: add the missing control types to MD_UIA_ROLES (Separator→SEPARATOR, TitleBar→LABEL to match the AT-SPI 'title bar' alias, HeaderItem→COLUMN_HEADER, Calendar→CALENDAR, AppBar→TOOL_BAR, SemanticZoom→LIST, Thumb/Custom→UNKNOWN explicitly), fix Header→PANEL, and log unmapped control types once per distinct id (mirror AXUI md-eiy). (c) Re-run the interactive Windows walk and the live suite: 0 multi-line compact nodes, unknown roles only for deliberate UNKNOWN mappings.
acceptance_criteria: Compact output never contains a newline inside a node line (unit test); Windows interactive dump shows no unmapped UIA control types except explicit UNKNOWN; Header no longer emits HDG; macOS + Linux + Windows suites pass.
close_reason: Merged to master. Compact labels sanitized (control chars -> single space, test added); UIA table: Separator/TitleBar/HeaderItem/Calendar/AppBar/SemanticZoom mapped, Thumb/Custom explicit UNKNOWN, Header->PANEL, once-per-type unmapped log. Verified live on Windows interactive session: 0 split lines (was 3), 2 unknown roles (was 5, both deliberate), 0 unmapped types logged; macOS 22/22, Linux 22/22 + live AT-SPI, Windows clang 0 diagnostics + MSVC /W4 clean.

title: AT-SPI backend leaves NULL holes in node->states for unmapped AtspiState values
description:
Why: src/core/a11y_atspi.c extract_states() sizes node->states to the full AtspiStateSet length (:75-76, calloc) but only strdup()s a name for the 17 AtspiState values in its switch (:87-109); every other state (ATSPI_STATE_HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, OPAQUE, MANAGES_DESCENDANTS, RESIZABLE, TRANSIENT, ...) leaves node->states[i] == NULL while state_count still counts it. Found on the Linux UTM VM (Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME 46) with MD_A11Y_LIVE_TESTS=1 ./build/test_atspi: 460 of 11776 checks fail at tests/test_atspi.c:372 (md_a11y_state_lookup(NULL) -> UNKNOWN) on a 15-node desktop; never reproducible on macOS. Consumers that iterate states[] without a NULL guard (any strcmp/cJSON_CreateString path) are at risk of a NULL deref; md_a11y_matches guards it, others need checking. Pre-existing — the pre-md-eiy code had the same 'if (name) states[i] = strdup(name)' pattern.

What: compact the array — append only mapped names and set state_count to the number appended (or realloc/shrink), never leave holes; optionally map a few more AT-SPI states that exist in a11y_vocab.h. Add a unit test with a fake state set containing unmapped values asserting no NULL entries and state_count == mapped count. Verify on the Linux VM: full suite + MD_A11Y_LIVE_TESTS=1 test_atspi must report 0 unknown states.
acceptance_criteria: Live AT-SPI test on the Linux VM reports 0 'unknown state' and PASSED; unit test covers unmapped states; no NULL entries possible in node->states from any backend.
close_reason: Merged to master as 623349a. extract_states compacts the array (no NULL holes); Linux-only seam md_atspi_extract_states + unit test with synthetic AtspiStateSet. Verified on the Linux UTM VM: 22/22, live AT-SPI PASSED 11326 checks / 0 unknown states (was 460 failures). macOS 22/22.

title: MCP bridge destroy does not unsubscribe a11y change callback (use-after-free on teardown)
description:
Why: md_mcp_bridge_create() registers md_mcp_a11y_change_cb with the bridge (or its resource ctx) as userdata via md_a11y_subscribe_changes(config->a11y, ...) (src/core/mcp_bridge.c:98). md_mcp_bridge_destroy() (mcp_bridge.c:173-) tears down transports, tool contexts, server, and agent but never detaches that subscription, and src/core/a11y.h exposes no unsubscribe API at all (only int (*subscribe_changes) in the vtable and md_a11y_subscribe_changes). Because the host keeps the MdA11yCtx alive and destroys it only after the bridge (src/host/main.c ~:790), any backend change event delivered in that window — AT-SPI event, AXObserver notification, UIA COM event — invokes the callback with a freed bridge/resource pointer. Surfaced by the md-52m engineer while adding snapshot invalidation to the callback (which widens the window since the callback now touches the snapshot too).

What: (1) add md_a11y_unsubscribe_changes(MdA11yCtx*, MdA11yChangeCb, void*) (or make subscribe return a handle) to a11y.h and implement it in all three backends — a11y_atspi.c (atspi_event_listener_deregister), a11y_axui.m (AXObserverRemoveNotification / CFRunLoopRemoveSource), a11y_uia.cpp (RemoveAutomationEventHandler / RemoveFocusChangedEventHandler); the backends must guarantee no callback runs after unsubscribe returns (join or synchronize with the dispatch thread). (2) Call it first thing in md_mcp_bridge_destroy(), before freeing anything the callback can touch. (3) Test in tests/test_mcp.c with the fake backend: after bridge destroy, firing a fake change event must not invoke the callback (use a counting hook).
acceptance_criteria: a11y.h has an unsubscribe API implemented by all three backends; md_mcp_bridge_destroy unsubscribes before teardown; test asserts no callback after destroy; all tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master as 39f2458 (93d07b9, 05b5c0d, 9a0240e). md_a11y_unsubscribe_changes with in-flight drain; bridge detaches first. UIA backend change uncompiled on macOS — verify on a Windows build. 22/22 unit + live AX test pass

title: Spike: run metadesk host/client inside containers (headless capture, input, FIPS, OCI runtime)
description:
Why: metadesk should run inside containers — both a containerized HOST (expose a container's desktop/app to agents + humans) and a containerized CLIENT (esp. agent/MCP). This is a runtime/architecture problem distinct from the packaging-format spike (md-kb7); md-kb7 only owns 'publish OCI images' as a distribution channel, this spike owns 'make it actually work headless in a container'. Strongly aligned with the AI-agent use case: a sandboxed container workload an agent drives headlessly via MCP + a11y.

What (spike — prototype + recommend):
- HOST in container:
  - Capture without a physical display: headless Wayland compositor (wlroots/cage/gnome headless), Xvfb+X11 capture, or a nested compositor; vs host-socket passthrough.
  - PipeWire + xdg-desktop-portal inside the container (own instance vs bind-mounting host sockets), ScreenCast consent in a non-interactive/headless context (restore_token, or portal backend that auto-grants).
  - Input injection without bare-metal /dev/uinput + CAP: wlroots virtual-pointer/virtual-keyboard protocols, ydotool, or inject into the nested compositor; device passthrough tradeoffs.
  - AT-SPI accessibility bus inside the container.
  - FIPS: TUN in the container netns (CAP_NET_ADMIN, /dev/net/tun) vs a FIPS sidecar sharing the network namespace; or direct IP only.
- CLIENT in container:
  - Agent/MCP client (no display) — primary, mostly networking.
  - Human client with display — GPU/display passthrough (DRI, Wayland/X socket) or stream-to-browser; likely out of initial scope.
- Runtime targets: Docker, Podman (incl. rootless), Kubernetes (Pod spec, securityContext, device plugins, service exposure), systemd-nspawn.
- Security: minimize capabilities, rootless where possible, document the privilege each feature requires.
- Reference deployments: Dockerfile(s)/compose + a k8s manifest for the headless-agent host scenario.

Deliverable: a design doc (docs/designs/) with a recommended headless-capture + input + FIPS architecture per runtime, a capability/privilege matrix, the consent/permission story for non-interactive hosts, example Dockerfile/compose/k8s manifests, and a phased plan with spin-off issues. Coordinate with md-kb7 (OCI images as a channel) and md-5zi (add container cells to the E2E matrix).
notes: 2026-11-16: all §7.4 decisions made — Q1 throwaway bundle; Q2 Host/Origin + bearer + NIP-98 (§7.7); Q3 explicit 127.0.0.1; Q4 exit on a11y loss + restart policy; Q5 unregister tools + is_error backstop; Q6 Tier A + proxy (W3) then binary-session (W3v); Q7 K8s deferred to Tier B. Work items filed as md-ah9.1–.14 (index in plan §1.1). md-ah9 itself = P0 (deploy/containers drafts still to do).

title: Spike: cross-platform distribution packaging — no-build-from-source install on all major platforms (incl. Omarchy)
description:
Why: today metadesk is source-only (meson + ninja, with a hand-built nostrc tree and system FFmpeg/SDL2/libyuv/etc.). Adoption requires simple, no-compile installs — users should get a signed, pre-built package per platform, not a build environment. ('non-FYC' = not 'fetch-your-compiler'/from-source.)

What (spike — survey, prototype, and recommend; not full build-out):
- Define per-platform packaging + delivery channels:
  - macOS: signed + notarized .app in a .dmg; Homebrew cask. (metadesk-host + metadesk-client.)
  - Windows: signed installer (MSI/EXE or MSIX) + winget manifest.
  - Linux (distro-agnostic): Flatpak on Flathub (portal/PipeWire/ScreenCast fit GNOME well) and/or AppImage for portable use.
  - Debian/Ubuntu: .deb + apt repo/PPA.
  - Fedora/RHEL: .rpm + Copr/dnf repo.
  - Arch + Omarchy: AUR package (pacman); validate on Omarchy's Hyprland/Wayland stack (xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland for ScreenCast, wlroots input).
- Dependency strategy: bundle vs system for FFmpeg, SDL2, libyuv, secp256k1, libwebsockets, cJSON, libb2, nostrc (currently an uninstalled build-tree dep — needs a proper installable/vendored story), and the GUI toolkit if the UX spike (md-70v) adds one.
- External runtime deps that are NOT bundled: the FIPS daemon (document how users get it per platform) and screen-capture permissions/portals per OS.
- Code signing / notarization / reproducibility; versioning; auto-update strategy (Sparkle/winget/Flatpak/repo updates).
- CI/CD: a release pipeline that builds + signs + publishes artifacts for every target from tags.

title: Spike: host/client management UX — identity/keys, connecting to hosts, address book, parity with remote-desktop tools
description:
Why: the current client/host are CLI-only (npub/IP args, op:// secrets, manual signer flags). To be usable like mainstream remote-desktop packages (RustDesk, Parsec, AnyDesk, RealVNC, Moonlight), metadesk needs real management UX for identity and connections on BOTH ends.

What (spike — explore + propose, not full build):
- Identity & key handling: generate/import/rotate Nostr keypairs (nsec/npub), secure at-rest storage (keychain/1Password/secret-service), unlock flow, display npub/fingerprint, signer selection (NIP-46 bunker, NIP-55L, NIP-5F, local).
- Connect-to-host flow: enter/scan an npub or IP, trust-on-first-use prompt, saved credentials, connection status/errors surfaced clearly (FIPS readiness, auth, route).
- Host address book: named saved hosts (npub/IP, last-connected, tags, per-host capabilities/notes), favorites, quick-connect, import/export.
- Host side: approve/deny incoming clients, NIP-51 allowlist management UI, session list/kick, per-client granted capabilities.
- General parity: settings (resolution/bitrate/fps), reconnect UX, clipboard, multi-monitor selection, in-overlay connection manager.

Deliverable: a design doc (docs/designs/) covering IA, flows, where it lives (ImGui overlay vs separate GTK/native app vs both), data model for the address book, security model for key storage, and a phased implementation plan with issues to spin off. Survey 2-3 comparable tools for UX patterns.
design:
Nostr-native constraint: prefer Nostr protocol primitives over bespoke mechanisms wherever practical.

- NIP-05: human-readable host identifiers (user@domain) that resolve to the host npub, so users connect to 'host@example.com' instead of a raw npub. Support NIP-05 verification/display in the connect flow and address book.
- NIP-51 (lists): use standard list events for the host allowlist/approved clients and for the client-side host address book / favorites / tags (e.g. categorized people/relay/app-specific sets) rather than a local-only format. Lists sync across a user's devices via relays.
- NIP-78 (application-specific data, kind 30078): store metadesk app/config data and address-book/host metadata as replaceable app-data events, so settings and saved hosts follow the identity across devices.
- NIP-44: encrypt any private payloads (address book contents, per-host notes/credentials, app-data, non-public list entries) with NIP-44 before publishing to relays. Nothing sensitive leaves the device in cleartext.
- Keep the existing session-negotiation stack (NIP-44-encrypted DMs, NIP-17 where applicable) and signer abstractions (NIP-46/55L/5F) as the identity/signing backbone.

Design doc must map each UX feature to the Nostr primitive it uses (and justify any case where a non-Nostr/local mechanism is chosen instead), plus relay strategy (which relays, user-configurable, NIP-65 outbox considerations) and offline/first-run behavior when no relay is reachable.
notes: 2026-11-16 decision (user): metadesk supports a signer interface like Groundhog/GNostr and lets the user decide which key is used for what. Design: signer accounts (backend,pubkey,label) over MdSigner backends 55L/5F/46; user-assigned host + client role bindings (same account may fill both); FIPS hosting validates host-role key == FIPS node key; NIP-46 creds in Secret Service/Keychain (Groundhog GhNip46CredentialStore pattern) — persistent NIP-46 pairing now in scope; CLI binding for headless hosts. Mirrors Groundhog GhAccountController in plain-C core (src/core/accounts.c). New work item P2.7. See docs/plans/management-ux-2026-11-14.md §7.6.

title: Testing: end-to-end host↔client matrix across Windows/GNOME/macOS/Omarchy over IP and FIPS
description:
Why: metadesk host/client has been exercised mostly on a single pairing (macOS client ↔ Ubuntu/GNOME VM host over direct IP). We need a documented, repeatable end-to-end test matrix that covers every supported platform as both host and client, over both transports, so regressions in capture, encode/decode, a11y, input injection, session negotiation, and FIPS routing are caught.

What: Define and run an E2E matrix.
- Roles × platforms: each of {Windows, GNOME/Linux, macOS, Omarchy (Hyprland/Wayland Linux)} as HOST and as CLIENT.
- Transports: (a) direct IP (LAN/IPv6 over TUN-less path), (b) FIPS mesh (npub, NIP-44 session negotiation, TCP over FIPS TUN).
- Per-cell checks: connect/auth, video (frames flow, correct dims, fills window, no trails), decode/FPS/bitrate, overlay, HUMAN input (mouse move/button/scroll + keyboard, correct button mapping, 1:1 cursor mapping), AGENT path (MCP tools, a11y tree, action-by-id), reconnect/restore, clean teardown.
- Capture consent/permissions per platform (ScreenCaptureKit TCC, PipeWire portal/restore_token, DXGI, Omarchy/Hyprland portal).

Acceptance: a results matrix (pass/fail + notes per cell), repeatable run steps/scripts, and a filed bug per failing cell. Note known-flaky areas (GNOME screencast restore, see md-3nv) explicitly.

title: client/host mouse: left-click sent as right-click; cursor X diverges when window != frame size
description:
Two mouse bugs found testing macOS client <-> Ubuntu VM:

1. Left click registered as right-click: uinput_mouse_button() uses 0=left,1=right,2=middle, but the client wire sends 1=left and the host handler called md_input_click(...,1) => BTN_RIGHT. Fixed: host maps wire buttons {1=left,2=mid,3=right} to md_input {0=left,2=mid,1=right}.

2. Remote cursor X diverges from the client cursor, growing with distance from the origin: map_to_remote() used the renderer's stored window size (set to the frame size by ensure_texture), but when the OS keeps the window at a different size than the frame (e.g. not shrunk to 1280 while the video is stretched to fill a 1512-wide window), mouse coords (0..1512) were divided by the stale 1280 -> remote moved ~1.18x too fast. Fixed: map_to_remote() now uses the live SDL_GetWindowSize, matching the space the video is stretched into and the space SDL reports mouse events in. Verified via libinput that the host uinput absolute mapping is itself linear/correct.
close_reason: Fixed: host button-convention mapping (left no longer right-click); client map_to_remote uses live SDL_GetWindowSize so cursor tracks when window!=frame. Host uinput mapping verified linear via libinput.

title: host: streaming unreliable across client reconnects and restored screencast sessions
description:
Two failure modes seen bringing up the macOS client against an Ubuntu VM host:

1. MULTI-CLIENT STALL: on each client disconnect the host calls md_encoder_flush(), which sends avcodec_send_frame(NULL) (EOF) to the PERSISTENT encoder. The next client's md_encoder_submit then fails silently (encoder in draining/EOF state) -> frames=0 sent=0, black client. Fresh single-client start works; the 2nd+ client gets nothing.

2. RESTORED-SCREENCAST IDLE: a PipeWire screencast restored via restore_token sometimes comes up with its node idle / unlinked, so capture delivers no frames even though md_capture_start succeeded (host frames=0 with a client connected). A fresh interactive consent streams reliably.

Hardening: (a) don't flush the persistent encoder to EOF per client; force a keyframe for each new client instead so they get an immediate IDR; (b) make pw_stop tear down per-start resources so md_capture_stop+start is a clean restart; (c) add a host capture watchdog that restarts capture when no frames arrive for several seconds while a client is connected, and after repeated failures clears the saved restore_token so the next start re-prompts for consent.
notes: Implemented: (a) encoder no longer flushed to EOF per client; force-keyframe on new connect (encode.c/h, host); (b) pw_stop tears down stream/core/portal so md_capture_stop+start restarts cleanly; (c) host capture watchdog restarts capture on stall and clears restore_token after repeated failures (capture.h/c vtable + pw_forget_authorization). Watchdog + token-clear verified live on the VM (restart x2 then cleared token with operator guidance). Multi-client frame-flow not live-verified this session — the GNOME screencast restore_token proved flaky and fresh consent requires an interactive click that wasn't available; encoder-EOF root cause is proven and unit tests pass 21/21.

title: client overlay: dragging broken (vertical-only + jump) from mismatched video/overlay render scale
description: After the single-present change, md_renderer_begin_frame drew the video at SDL scale 1.0 with a pixel viewport while render_draw_data drew the overlay at scale 2.0 (DisplayFramebufferScale). ImGui lays out and hit-tests in logical points; drawing the overlay in a different effective space than ImGui expected made the panel's grab math wrong — the title bar could only be dragged vertically and jumped ~50px on mousedown. Fix: render the whole frame (video + overlay) in one space — begin_frame sets a full-output viewport then the HiDPI scale, draws the video to a point-sized dst, and render_draw_data no longer touches the scale.
close_reason: Fixed in unified-coordinate render; verified live: overlay drags correctly in both axes with no jump, video still fills window

title: host: PipeWire screencast needs interactive consent every run (no restore_token)
description: portal_screencast_open() requested persist_mode=0, so every host start shows the GNOME 'Share your screen' dialog; unattended, the Start call times out after 60s and capture falls back to a no-op direct connect (frames=0, black client). Fix: request persist_mode=2 and persist the returned restore_token under XDG_STATE_HOME, reusing it on later runs so consent is remembered after one approval.
close_reason: Fixed and verified live: video fills window, single-present (no trails), restore_token skips consent, mouse/keyboard forwarded (remote cursor tracks + hover responds, host rx grows)

title: client: human mouse/keyboard input is never forwarded to the host
description: The human video client displays the remote desktop but captures no input: there is no MD_PKT_INPUT packet, and client/main.c never translates SDL mouse/keyboard events into anything sent to the host. The host already has md_input wired (uinput/CGEvent/SendInput) via the agent, so only a raw-input packet + client capture + host injection are missing. Implement MD_PKT_INPUT carrying mouse move/button/wheel and key/text; forward on the client (skipping events ImGui consumes) mapped to remote coords; inject on the host via md_input_*.
close_reason: Fixed and verified live: video fills window, single-present (no trails), restore_token skips consent, mouse/keyboard forwarded (remote cursor tracks + hover responds, host rx grows)

title: MCP: add targeted a11y query tools and stop pinning tree format to JSON
description:
Why: an MCP agent today has exactly one way to read the UI tree — the whole metadesk://ui-tree resource (src/core/mcp_resources.c:26-56) — and the nine metadesk_* action tools (src/core/mcp_tools.c:315-333) return either a JSON delta or the whole tree. There is no node-level or filtered read path, so the model must scan every node to find a target, paying full token cost per read. The host also hard-pins MCP to MD_TREE_FORMAT_JSON (src/host/main.c:762), so the token-efficient compact format (md_a11y_to_compact, src/core/a11y.c:554) is never available to agents even though the bridge/resources already support it (mcp_resources.c:37-45). Considered and rejected: GraphQL over MCP — LLMs mis-author query strings, GraphQL has no recursive fragments for tree traversal, no lightweight C parser exists, and it would bypass MCP per-tool JSON Schema validation. Targeted tools over the existing MdA11yNode tree get ~90% of the value with zero new dependencies. Origin: docs/investigations/a11y-xml-ingestion-claim-2026-11-13.md follow-up discussion.

What:
1. New read tools in src/core/mcp_tools.c, all operating on md_a11y_walk() output (or a cached snapshot) with the existing serializers:
   - metadesk_find(role?, label_contains?, state?, limit=50, format=compact|json) — server-side filter; returns matching nodes (flat list, compact lines by default).
   - metadesk_subtree(id, depth=2, format) — scoped traversal rooted at a node id.
   - metadesk_node(id) — full JSON detail for one node (role, label, states, bounds, child count).
   - metadesk_focused() — the node carrying the 'focused' state plus its ancestor window.
   - metadesk_windows() — top-level windows/frames (role, label, id, bounds).
   Each tool gets a JSON Schema in its registration so arguments are validated by the MCP layer; shared helpers (find_node_by_id already exists in agent.c:47-57) should move to a11y.c or a small a11y_query.c rather than be duplicated.
2. Format pinning: remove the hard-coded MD_TREE_FORMAT_JSON at src/host/main.c:762. Make the MCP bridge default to compact for the ui-tree resource and tool text results, with a per-call 'format' argument on the read tools and a host CLI/config switch for the resource default. Keep application/json vs text/plain mimeType selection in mcp_resources.c:143-144 consistent with the chosen format.
3. Tests in tests/test_mcp.c: find by role/label/state with limit, subtree depth bounds, node-not-found error shape, focused/windows on a fixture tree, and resource mimeType matching the configured format.
4. Docs: add the new tools and the format switch to docs/AGENT_API.md and the MCP section of docs/metadesk-spec.md.

Depends on / interacts with: md-qqz (compact sessions get JSON deltas) — the compact default for MCP tool results must not reintroduce that mismatch; tool results that are deltas should stay JSON or be clearly discriminated. md-1kg (subscribe_changes unimplemented) — once live, agents should prefer pushed deltas + targeted reads over full re-reads.
acceptance_criteria: Five new read tools registered with JSON Schemas and covered by test_mcp; MD_TREE_FORMAT_JSON no longer hard-coded in src/host/main.c; MCP ui-tree resource and read tools default to compact with a working per-call/host override; mimeType matches format; AGENT_API.md documents the tools; all tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master as fdb4946; 5 read tools, a11y_query.{c,h}, --mcp-tree-format, review fixes in cd6c2c8; 22/22 tests

title: test_mcp_http: http_request single read() races header/body writes
description: tests/test_mcp_http.c http_request() does a single read(); mcp_http.c send_http_response() writes headers and body in separate write_all() calls, so the test can observe only the headers and fail the '"result"'/protocolVersion checks (test_post_initialize fails deterministically on macOS). title: Compact-format sessions receive JSON deltas the client cannot patch
description:
Why: agent_render_update_locked() (src/core/agent.c:220-244) and md_agent_send_delta() (agent.c:338-362) always emit JSON via md_a11y_delta_to_json() regardless of agent->tree_format. A client that negotiated MD_TREE_FORMAT_COMPACT (src/client/main.c:205,220) caches a compact plain-text snapshot in ctx.ui_tree_json (client/main.c:732-740) and then calls md_a11y_tree_patch() (client/main.c:760) which begins with cJSON_Parse(tree_json) (src/core/a11y.c:699) — the compact snapshot fails to parse, patch returns NULL, and the client silently keeps the stale tree. Spec docs/metadesk-spec.md §3.3.3 says deltas use 'the same formats above', which the implementation does not do.

Currently dormant: the stock video client never sends MD_PKT_ACTION, and the MCP host pins MD_TREE_FORMAT_JSON (src/host/main.c:762). It becomes active for any stream consumer that negotiates compact and submits actions.

What: (a) in agent.c, make the update policy format-aware — for compact sessions send a full compact snapshot (MD_PKT_UI_TREE) instead of a JSON delta, in both agent_render_update_locked() and md_agent_send_delta(); (b) correct spec §3.3.3 to document JSON deltas for JSON sessions and full-snapshot replacement for compact sessions (or design a real compact delta contract + consumer); (c) add a test in tests/test_agent.c covering a compact-negotiated agent after an action. Found during docs/investigations/a11y-xml-ingestion-claim-2026-11-13.md.
acceptance_criteria: Compact-negotiated agent never emits MD_PKT_UI_TREE_DELTA with JSON payload; spec §3.3.3 matches implementation; test_agent covers compact post-action update.
close_reason: Merged to master as 8129758 (commits 9864e03,12be22b for md-qqz; a365ef0,b1b665f for md-52m); 22/22 tests

title: nostrc/libfiber: add fiber-parking recvfrom/sendto/recvmsg/sendmsg
description:
Target repo: nostrc (libgo/fiber). Filed here because metadesk is the consumer and the investigation lives in nostrc docs/investigations/fips-rust-to-c-port-on-nostrc-2026-11-13.md (branch feature/fips).

Why: libfiber's netpoller-aware I/O surface is only gof_read, gof_write, gof_connect and gof_accept (libgo/fiber/include/libgo/fiber.h). There is no datagram API: a fiber doing UDP must either block the worker thread on recvfrom/sendmsg or hand-roll the park/wake cycle. Any FIPS-style UDP transport (per-peer connected sockets, IP_PKTINFO/IP_RECVDSTADDR, ECN/CE via recvmsg cmsg, SO_BINDTODEVICE/IP_BOUND_IF) and SCM_RIGHTS fd passing (the FIPS native datagram API) need sendmsg/recvmsg. metadesk's own future UDP media path over fibers would hit the same wall.

What: add gof_recvfrom, gof_sendto, gof_recvmsg and gof_sendmsg to libfiber mirroring gof_read's park-on-EAGAIN/resume-on-readiness pattern (with the optional timeout_ms the connect/accept wrappers already take), cover them in libgo/fiber/tests (test_io.c / test_io_timeout.c), and document the UDP story in libgo/fiber/README.md 'Fiber-friendly I/O'.
acceptance_criteria: gof_recvfrom/gof_sendto/gof_recvmsg/gof_sendmsg exist, park the fiber instead of the worker, pass an epoll and a kqueue test, and are documented in the fiber README

title: Update FIPS runtime contract to 0.6.x and add /var/run/fips control socket path
description:
Why: docs/investigations/fips-rust-to-c-port-on-nostrc-2026-11-13.md (nostrc, branch feature/fips) re-verified metadesk against fips@6aa80504 (v0.6.0-dev) and found two drifts in the external FIPS runtime contract.

1. docs/metadesk-spec.md §2.2.1 still says 'Upstream FIPS v0.3.x / v0.4.x'; fips tags run through v0.5.3 and master is 0.6.0-dev. Re-check the listed capabilities (show_status/show_peers/show_sessions, node.discovery.nostr.* keys — fips now spells these node.rendezvous.nostr.*) against docs/reference/control-socket.md and docs/reference/configuration.md in fips.

2. fips resolves its control socket as: /run/fips/control.sock → /var/run/fips/control.sock (macOS and FreeBSD only, created by the LaunchDaemon / rc.d service) → $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fips/control.sock → /tmp/fips-control.sock. src/core/fips_control.h defines only MD_FIPS_CONTROL_RUN_SOCKET (/run/fips), MD_FIPS_CONTROL_XDG_SUFFIX and MD_FIPS_CONTROL_TMP_SOCKET, so a packaged macOS daemon is never found and metadesk reports DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE.

What: add the /var/run/fips step to md_fips_control_resolve_socket_path on macOS/FreeBSD in the same order fips uses, extend tests/test_fips_control.c for it, and update spec §2.2.1 (version, socket order, config key names).
acceptance_criteria: fips_control resolves /var/run/fips/control.sock on macOS/FreeBSD between /run/fips and XDG; test_fips_control covers the new step; spec §2.2.1 names 0.6.x and the four-step socket order
close_reason: Implemented and merged: metadesk master e217b33 (md-bm1); nostrc master 7f27d073f via feature/libgo-swap 9f72fc109 (md-o74) and feature/libfiber-datagram-io 6830759b1 (md-ts4), libgo 0.2.0 -> 0.3.0

title: UIA tree walk is ~3-5 ms/node: batch property reads with IUIAutomationCacheRequest
description:
Why: the first interactive Windows walk (Win11 ARM64 UTM VM) took 729-1155 ms for 250 nodes. a11y_uia.cpp walk_element() makes several cross-process COM calls per element (get_CurrentControlType, get_CurrentName, state properties, get_CurrentBoundingRectangle, runtime id, plus TreeWalker GetFirstChild/GetNextSibling). A real desktop with a browser or IDE open is thousands of nodes -> multi-second snapshots. Since md-ayo, walks happen only on reads (lazy MCP snapshot), not per event, so this is latency for agent reads rather than CPU burn — hence P3.

What: build one IUIAutomationCacheRequest with the properties walk_element needs (ControlType, Name, BoundingRectangle, IsEnabled, HasKeyboardFocus, IsOffscreen, toggle/selection/expand states as used by extract_states, RuntimeId) and TreeScope_Subtree (or Element+Children per level), then use FindAllBuildCache / GetCachedChildren and get_Cached* accessors. Keep the existing MAX_DEPTH/MAX_CHILDREN bounds. Measure before/after on the Windows VM with atspi_dump --compact run in the interactive session (scheduled task with interactive logon — see bd memory windows-vm-testing).
acceptance_criteria: Same compact/JSON output as the uncached walk on the same desktop; >=3x faster walk measured on the Windows VM; live UIA suite passes.

title: test_sse_stalled_client flaky under parallel test execution
description:
Why: tests/test_mcp_http.c test_sse_stalled_client (added in md-ed7, commit e9dfcc5/01291fe) fails or times out when the MCP suites are run in parallel on a loaded host (observed during md-ayo verification: 4 failures + 1 suite timeout in a parallel 10x repeat; assertions around tests/test_mcp_http.c:610/614/632). The same tests pass 10/10 when run serially. The test fills a kernel socket buffer to simulate a stalled SSE reader and asserts the stalled client is dropped within sse_write_timeout_ms while a healthy client keeps receiving; under CPU contention the timing window and the buffer-fill heuristics become scheduling-dependent.

What: make the test deterministic rather than timing-based — e.g. use a tiny SO_SNDBUF / SO_RCVBUF on the stalled client's socket pair so the buffer fills with a known small number of bytes, drive the write deadline with an injectable clock or a very short timeout plus a generous assertion window, and wait on observable state (client count drops; healthy client receives event N) with latch_wait instead of elapsed-time bounds. Also consider marking the HTTP suite is_parallel: false in meson.build as a stopgap if it remains sensitive. Logs from the failing run were under /tmp/md-ayo-*.log on the dev host (ephemeral).
acceptance_criteria: MCP HTTP suite passes 20/20 when the four MCP suites are run concurrently (meson test --num-processes 4 looped) on the dev host; no wall-clock bounds in test_sse_stalled_client.
close_reason: Merged to master as 837f3b1 (31c8256, 5a8d461). test_sse_stalled_client is state-based: pre-connect SO_RCVBUF on clients, sse_sndbuf test knob (SSE sockets only, 0 = untouched) bounds server-side buffering so all stalled clients overflow on the first broadcast; broadcast-until-count==1 with 1024-frame cap; 5->1 within one write asserted via count snapshots; single readiness probe; concurrent healthy reader terminated by sentinel; EOF confirmation 2s each. Remaining md_now_ms pass/fail bounds removed from HTTP/stdio tests; stdio memcmp fixed (json+queued, non-uniform payload). Verified: 22/22, 20x --num-processes 4 (80/80), 20x HTTP under 4 CPU burners (20/20), +3x parallel on merge. macOS only; Linux buffer accounting reasoned, not run.

title: MCP bridge shutdown can block on a stuck transport write inside the a11y change callback
description:
Why: after md-6h0, md_mcp_bridge_destroy() first calls md_a11y_unsubscribe_changes(), which waits for any in-flight md_mcp_a11y_change_cb to return (src/core/a11y.c change_clear_and_drain). That callback calls md_mcp_notify_tree_changed(server) -> server write_fn -> md_mcp_http_write / md_mcp_stdio_write. If the SSE client has stalled, or stdout is a full pipe whose reader is gone (SIGPIPE ignored), the write blocks, the drain never completes, and destroy never reaches md_mcp_http_destroy / md_mcp_stdio_destroy — the only things that would unblock the write. Pre-existing class of problem (a blocked write also wedged the event thread before md-6h0); the drain just makes it surface at shutdown. Found in code review of fix/md-6h0-a11y-unsubscribe.

What: give the bridge a shutdown sequence that cannot wedge: (a) add md_mcp_server_detach_transport() (or make write_fn a no-op) so notifications become drop-on-floor once shutdown starts; call it BEFORE the drain, then destroy transports, then drain, then free; or (b) make the transport writes non-blocking / bounded (poll with timeout, drop notification on timeout) so a callback can never block indefinitely. Prefer (b) for the SSE path since a stalled client should never stall the host regardless of shutdown. Test: fake write_fn that blocks on a semaphore; call md_mcp_bridge_destroy from another thread; assert it returns within a bound after the transport is torn down.
acceptance_criteria: md_mcp_bridge_destroy returns within a bounded time with a change callback blocked in write_fn; no UAF (run under ASan); existing tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master as 9cb539f (d216ead, e9dfcc5, 01291fe). Bounded SSE/POST/stdio writes (SO_SNDTIMEO, poll-deadline helper in io_util), server quiesce + sink_mu before a11y drain, SSE admission fix. 22/22 unit, MCP suites x10, ASan clean on macOS

title: MCP read tools: serve from cached a11y snapshot instead of full walk per call
description:
Why: the md-n68 read tools (metadesk_find/subtree/node/focused/windows in src/core/mcp_tools.c) each perform a fresh md_a11y_walk() — a full desktop traversal (thousands of D-Bus round trips on AT-SPI) — even for single-node lookups. An agent doing find -> node -> subtree -> click walks the desktop four times for an unchanged UI. MdAgent already keeps cached_tree for target resolution (src/core/agent.c), and the bridge registers a change subscription (src/core/mcp_bridge.c) that could invalidate a shared snapshot.

What: introduce one bridge-owned snapshot (mutex-protected) shared by the agent's target resolution, the ui-tree resource, and the read tools; invalidate it after actions and on md_mcp_a11y_change_cb; refresh lazily on next read. Keep md_a11y_walk semantics for the stream path unchanged. Also fold in the smaller review nits from md-n68: build compact find output into one StrBuf instead of a temporary cJSON string array; make read-tool validation errors name the offending field (as extract_args does for action tools); consider strcasecmp/strcasestr vs the hand-rolled equal_ci/contains_ci (keep hand-rolled only if MSVC portability is the reason, and say so in a comment).

Depends on md-1kg (subscribe_changes) for correct invalidation on Linux/macOS/Windows; without it, snapshot staleness is bounded only by post-action invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: Read tools and ui-tree resource share one snapshot; a find->node->subtree sequence on an unchanged UI performs one walk (assert via a counting fake backend in test_mcp); snapshot invalidated after any action tool and on change callback; all tests pass.

title: host --bind rejects IPv4 literals with misleading 'failed to bind' error
description: md_stream_server_create_tls() parses --bind only via inet_pton(AF_INET6). title: nostrc/libgo: atomic snapshot-swap helper (watch/ArcSwap analogue) over refptr
description:
Target repo: nostrc (libgo). Filed here because metadesk is the consumer; see docs/investigations/fips-rust-to-c-port-on-nostrc-2026-11-13.md §5.3 in nostrc (branch feature/fips).

Why: libgo has channels, select, contexts, wait groups and refptr, but no primitive for 'many readers take a consistent snapshot of a value a writer replaces wholesale'. Rust code of the kind metadesk may port or mirror uses tokio::sync::watch (20 sites in fips) and arc_swap::ArcSwap (58 sites) for exactly this: config reload, peer tables, routing snapshots read on hot paths without a lock. Today the C options are a mutex around a pointer (contention on hot reads) or a hand-rolled _Atomic pointer with ad-hoc refcount discipline per call site.

What: add a small libgo type (e.g. GoSwap) holding an _Atomic(void*) to a refptr-managed value with go_swap_load (retain + return), go_swap_store (publish new, release old), and optionally a GoChannel notification for watch-style wakeups; tests under libgo/tests including a TSan run; document in libgo/LIBGO.md.
acceptance_criteria: GoSwap (or equivalent) lands in libgo with load/store semantics that never free a value a reader still holds, a stress test passes under TSan, and LIBGO.md documents it
